title: Epidural morphine combined with femoral nerve block for postoperative analgesia
author: Zhao-Ting Meng
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wanfade

steps.title: Screen and consent patients
steps.instruction: Screen patients the day before surgery, obtain written informed consent and enroll eligible participants.

steps.title: Collect baseline patient data
steps.instruction: Record demographic characteristics, diagnosis, comorbidities, current medications, NYHA class, ASA class, prior surgery/anesthesia history, and relevant laboratory results.

steps.title: Randomize and prepare study drugs
steps.instruction: Randomize patients 1:1 with block size 4 using SAS 9.3; assign a recruitment number; a study coordinator prepares either 2 mg morphine in 5 mL normal saline or 5 mL normal saline, places each in identical 5 mL syringes labeled with the recruitment number, seals in sequentially numbered letters and stores until study end.

steps.title: Perform combined spinal‑epidural anesthesia
steps.instruction: Administer combined spinal anesthesia with 0.5 % hyperbaric bupivacaine and epidural anesthesia with 2 % lidocaine; the anesthesiologist determines the exact dosages.

steps.title: Provide intra‑operative dexmedetomidine
steps.instruction: Start dexmedetomidine infusion after hemodynamic stability post‑spinal: loading dose 0.4 µg/kg over 10 min, then maintenance 0.2 µg/kg/h; stop infusion before the end of surgery.

steps.title: Administer study drug via epidural
steps.instruction: At the end of surgery, inject the prepared study drug (morphine or saline) through the indwelling epidural catheter, then remove the catheter.

steps.title: Transfer to PACU and block femoral nerve
steps.instruction: Move the patient to the post‑anesthetic care unit; perform a single‑injection femoral nerve block with 20 mL of 0.5 % ropivacaine under ultrasound and nerve‑stimulator guidance.

steps.title: Set up PCIA pump
steps.instruction: Connect a patient‑controlled intravenous analgesia pump containing 100 mL of 0.5 mg/mL morphine; program a 2 mL bolus, lockout interval 8–10 min, background infusion 0.5 mL/h; stop the pump at 48 h post‑surgery and, if emptied earlier, replace with supplemental morphine of the same concentration to maintain 48 h coverage.

steps.title: Monitor in PACU
steps.instruction: Observe the patient for at least 30 min; assess lower‑limb motor block using the modified Bromage scale at PACU arrival and again at 30 min.

steps.title: Record intra‑operative data
steps.instruction: Document duration of anesthesia and surgery, type of surgery, doses of all anesthetic drugs, and intra‑operative fluid balance.

steps.title: Post‑operative follow‑up assessments
steps.instruction: Visit patients at 6, 12, 24, 36, and 48 h (±1 h). At each visit assess pain at rest and with movement using an 11‑point NRS, evaluate motor block with the Bromage scale, count PCIA bolus deliveries since the previous visit, record side effects (nausea, vomiting, pruritus, dizziness), note any additional analgesics and their doses, measure drainage volume, and note any blood transfusion. At 48 h record patient satisfaction (1 = poor to 4 = excellent).

steps.title: Document additional postoperative outcomes
steps.instruction: Record time to ambulation, length of postoperative hospital stay, any complications occurring within 30 days, and 30‑day mortality.

steps.title: Thirty‑day follow‑up
steps.instruction: At 30 days post‑surgery, assess quality of life with the 12‑item Short‑Form (SF‑12) and arthritic symptoms with the WOMAC osteoarthritis index; conduct a face‑to‑face interview during the patient’s routine re‑examination visit.
